answer:
The file `/home/hyoklee/cae_test_data/porotomo/dasv_native_PoroTomo_iDAS025_160318160317.h5` (46,590,272 bytes) contains **8 datasets**:

| Path | Shape | Dtype | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/das` | (30000, 384) | float32 | strain; chunked (2000, 384); sampling interval 0.001 s — the main DAS data |
| `/t` | (30000,) | float64 | time axis, seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z (2016-03-18T10:03:17.99 → 10:03:47.99 UTC, 30 s window) |
| `/trace` | (30000,) | int64 | trace number, 0–29999 |
| `/channel` | (384,) | int32 | channel number, 1–384 |
| `/x` | (384,) | float32 | Easting (UTM zone 11N, ~327962–327961 m) |
| `/y` | (384,) | float32 | Northing (~4407555 m) |
| `/z` | (384,) | float32 | Elevation above ellipsoid, 866–1230 m |
| `/crs` | scalar | uint8 | CRS metadata (EPSG:32611, WGS 84 / UTM 11N) as attributes |

So the core measurement is `/das`: 30,000 time samples × 384 fiber channels of strain at 1 kHz, with `/t` and `/trace` as the time/trace axes and `/channel`, `/x`, `/y`, `/z` describing the 384 sensor locations along the fiber. Root attributes follow the DAS-HDF5-1.0 / CF-1.7 conventions, from instrument iDAS025 (source SEG-Y `PoroTomo_iDAS025_160318160317.sgy`, PoroTomo project at Brady Hot Springs).
